in_arabic.name: تَهَمْتان
in_arabic.meaning: الاسم يعني الشخص الذي يمتلك الحكمة والشجاعة
in_arabic.long_meaning: تَهَمْتان هو اسم عربي قديم يعود إلى العصور الإسلامية، ويعود أصل الكلمة إلى اللغة الفارسية، ويشير إلى الشخص الذي يتمتع بالحكمة والشجاعة، ويتميز بالصبر والثبات في مواجهة التحديات، وله أهمية كبيرة في الثقافة الإسلامية sebagai رمز للقوة والسلطة

in_urdu.name: تہمتان

data.cultural_impact: The name "Tahamtan" is derived from the Arabic language, specifically the term "al-Tahammadvat" which means "the quest for justice", emphasizing a strong moral character and a commitment to truth and fairness in personal and professional relationships. In Islamic culture, the pursuit of justice and fairness is highly valued and deeply embedded in the teachings of the Koran and Hadith. As the name "Tahamtan" suggests, an individual bearing this name would be expected to uphold these values in their daily lives and interactions with others, contributing positively to their community and society as a whole.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, the name "Tahamtan" carries deep spiritual significance as it reflects the divine attributes of mercy, compassion, and benevolence. It is believed that by striving for justice and fairness, one is not only fulfilling a moral obligation but also drawing closer to God, who is the ultimate source of justice and fairness. Thus, the name "Tahamtan" serves as a constant reminder of the importance of living in accordance with these Islamic values, fostering a strong spiritual connection between the individual and their Almighty Creator.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Tahamtan was a Persian vizier during the late Sassanid Empire. The name Tahamtan carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Sassanid Empire was the last pre-Islamic Persian Empire, ruling from 224 to 651 AD. Tahamtan served as a vizier during the reign of Emperor Khosrow I Anushirvan.
